First, welcome to /v/flashfiction !

This subverse is a place to share very short stories that you have either written, or stumbled across on the internet. Flash fiction is known under other descriptions such as micro fiction, short short stories, sudden stories and my personal favorite, postcard stories. Since there are no strict rules on what constitutes flash fiction you may find yourself wondering if your story belongs here or on a sub that is dedicated to short stories. The best way to deal with this is to not. Short stories and flash fiction have a lot in common. My personal rule of thumb is to take into consideration whether a reader would take the time to read my story if it appeared in a magazine. If the answer is yes, it's probably flash fiction.

If you are going to submit an original story, please use the DISCUSS button. If you are going to link to a story that is hosted on another site, your own or otherwise, please use the SHARE A LINK button.

Thank you and enjoy your stay.

I've found that sellers of humanely treated meat tend to jump on every possible bandwagon from gluten free to organic. It occurs to me that as someone who doesn't care about those things there may be a seller who only certifies for the humane treatment of their animals. Unfortunately I have no idea where (what store) to look for such. Can improperly treated cattle be sold as kosher? i.e. can kosher certification serve as de-facto humanity certification?

I looked for certifying organizations online but I couldn't find an easy-to-shop-for label. They exist but I've never seen one in the wild.

If so this still leaves the question of pigs. I like the occasional pork chop. Where should I be shopping?
Where to buy humanely treated meat?

Your best bet is looking for a local butcher that works only with small, family-run farms in the area. You pay extra, but for me there's no alternative. I'm not comfortable with the conditions that factory farms impose on their livestock. If you live in a reasonably-sized city, you'll almost certainly have a small butcher shop there. Mine has a map on the wall with the names of the ranches they do business with, so you can do your own research if you want to be sure.

So if you're in the U.S. of A. there is The Global Animal Partnership. Usually local CoOps will have a local rancher list that will show all the local ranchers and some info on them.

As far as Kosher is concerned, it mostly has to do with the religious aspects of the handling, rather than the health or welfare of the animal. The kosher butcher just has to slit the throat of the animal, check the lungs, and remove the suet and the big veins.

Temple Grandin, an autistic lady who became a leading advocate of animal compassion, changed most of the slaughter houses in the US to humane slaughtering. Before her, the slaughter houses used a lot of electric prods, forcing animals with broken legs through, and downed animals (sick animals). Europeans abide by the European Commission edicts on animal welfare, so are a bit ahead.

There is a big difference between ranchers, who are very concerned with the health of the animals, and the meat packing plants who are very concerned with the quality of the product. As Temple showed, a well treated animal provides much more profitable meat. With that said, the massive, prevalent use of anti-biotics and high density feed lots contributes greatly to, if not cruel, a unfulfilled life.

-20+ year butcher

In the third hour of the first night, it became apparent that the remaining guests wouldn't be arriving. A substantial deviation from the general consensus that arriving fashionably late is preferred. Perhaps the host won't mind the abundance of vacant seats surrounding the meticulously decorated mensa, but if it were a gathering of individuals put on by myself, I would have a generous fill of disappointment. No less, the evening was pressing on into the late hours, and the time had come to abandon hope of any stragglers. Now was the moment to seize, as the invitees were beginning to wind down and lose interest in one another. A female voice began to break through the drone of mumblings, demanding attention as it's tone slowly arose. It had become obvious she demanded the attention of the room, and that she would now command all conversation.

"Mr. Bear, and Lady Giraffe. I would like to thank you for attending my party. Daddy, would you please pour a cup of tea?"

I promptly adjusted the paper hat donned upon the crown of my head, lifted the pink kettle which contains an imaginary liquid, and began to pour it into the glasses of the aforementioned guests. Indeed, the wait was worthwhile, as these were the best tea parties I would ever attend.
